What happens here

This is QSC's first facility, dedicated to mechanical and electrical repair, diagnostics and scheduled care. Every visit starts with diagnosis and ends with a documented report.

The facility organizes its work around four zones: diagnostic bays where the car's systems are read and guided tests performed; general mechanical bays for engines, transmissions, brakes and suspension; the wheel-alignment and geometry station; and the scheduled-maintenance area where periodic services and multi-point inspections run. Each zone has its technicians and equipment, and a car moves between them according to what diagnosis reveals, not prior assumptions.

What customers feel from this organization is two things: speed to the cause, because the car goes straight to the right technician and equipment; and quality of documentation, because every station records what it found and did. At the end of the visit it all converges into one readable report: what was checked, what was found, what was done, and what deserves watching — the report that, over time, builds your car's file at QSC.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Why does QSC run two separate workshops?

Because the two crafts conflict in one building: dust from mechanical work is the enemy of paint, and paint operations have no place beside engine repair. Separate facilities mean each team, space and set of equipment serves one discipline done properly.

Which workshop should I go to?

Engine, gearbox, electrical, AC, diagnostics, suspension or scheduled service → the maintenance workshop. Paint, dents, scratches, collision or body damage → the painting & bodywork workshop. Unsure? Call the main line and the team routes you.

Can one workshop move my car to the other if it needs both?

Yes — transfers between the facilities are handled by QSC with the same documented handover as any pickup, and you are kept informed at each step.
